title: Sing Buri Cafes Ranked 2026 — 10 Town & Riverside Spots | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: Our ranked guide to 10 real, currently-open cafes in Sing Buri, Thailand — easy in-town spots, rice-field and riverside cafes, and ones beside temples. A handy rest stop after temple-hopping, with signature drinks, prices and opening hours.
keywords: Sing Buri cafes, Sing Buri coffee shops, riverside cafe Sing Buri, cafes in Sing Buri town
h1:
Sing Buri Cafes Ranked
In Town & by the River
intro: Sing Buri is a small town where you can spend the whole day temple-hopping. Once you've finished walking the temples, the sun's getting strong and your legs are tired, the best thing you can do is find a cool corner and sit down with a coffee. The town has cafes spread across the easy-to-reach market area, out by the green rice fields, in Thai-style houses set in gardens, and right next to temples. We've picked 10 places that are actually open right now, and we'll tell you straight which ones only open on weekends and which ones are good to drop into while you're doing the temple route.

blocks.html: The nice thing about Sing Buri's cafes is that they're not as packed as the big tourist towns. Most coffees start at 30–60 THB, parking is easy to find, and a lot of the cafes sit right on the temple-hopping route. We ranked them based on real review feedback, how easy they are to drop into between sights, and whether the atmosphere actually lets you sit and rest — not just snap a photo and leave.

items.name: Vazana Coffee House
items.blurb: A glass-house cafe set in a flower garden off Route 11 on the In Buri side. The indoor section is properly air-conditioned and cool, while the outdoor seating sits under shady trees. The standout drink is the honey cordyceps americano, and there's real savoury food too, like fish and chips and grilled pork neck. This is a place you can settle in for a while, not just stop for photos.
items.meta: In Buri · open daily 8.00–19.00 (closes later on Sat–Sun)

items.name: Loychai Eye View Cafe
items.blurb: An old Thai-style house set in a garden in Bang Man, close to the town centre. You can sit on the wooden veranda or under a big rain tree — the vibe is quiet, peaceful and shady. The menu covers coffee, cake, spaghetti and fried chicken wings. Good to know before you go: it only opens on Saturdays, Sundays and some public holidays, so check its Facebook page first.
items.meta: Bang Man, Mueang Sing Buri · open Sat–Sun (check the page first)

items.name: Retro Cafe at Wat Phikun Thong
items.blurb: A cafe inside Wat Phikun Thong in Tha Chang district, with views over a blue lotus pond and the large Buddha image. There's a Bali-style swing for photos. It's a really convenient stop if you're already visiting Wat Phikun Thong — just sit down for a coffee afterwards without driving anywhere else.
items.meta: Wat Phikun Thong, Tha Chang · open daily 9.30–19.30 (closed Wed)

items.name: The Green @ Singburi
items.blurb: A spacious riverside cafe whose decor changes with the seasons, with waterside seating to catch the breeze. It works as both a cafe and a restaurant, with dishes like khao man kai, khao soi, fried spring rolls and avocado smoothies. Good for a long, leisurely meal, but it only opens on Saturdays and Sundays, so plan your day around that.

items.name: Sip & Prost
items.blurb: An in-town spot on the Krungsri Bank soi, an easy walk from the market. It's a small open-air cafe with cute photo corners and friendly starting prices, good for a stop while you're wandering around town or before/after a bowl of noodles. There's even a colouring activity for kids.

items.name: Singkafe (Singburi Cafe)
items.blurb: A small coffee shop in the Sing Buri town market, decorated with wood and vintage pieces. The menu covers the basics — latte, cappuccino, mocha, green tea — at the lowest prices on this list, starting at 30 THB. Good for anyone on a tight budget who still wants a proper cup of coffee while walking the market.
items.meta: Sing Buri town market · near Ood Fresh Milk

items.name: WEEK.singburi
items.blurb: A minimalist white cafe in the Bang Rachan area, focused on coffee across several roasts, with dirty coffee, fruit-matcha drinks and brownies on the menu. Good for serious coffee drinkers who like a calm setting, and it sits right on the route to the Bang Rachan historical sites.

items.name: Rimna Cafe
items.blurb: A cafe set among the fields in the Bang Rachan area, with a long wooden bridge stretching out over the rice paddies for natural-looking photos. There's both an air-conditioned indoor section and outdoor seating, with easy-on-the-eyes green views. Best in the morning before it gets too hot.

items.name: De'champ Cafe
items.blurb: A modern cafe looking out over the rice fields, directly across from Wat Phikun Thong, making it another option for a rest after visiting the temple. The menu is straightforward — coffee, Thai tea and blueberry cheese pie — with low prices and an open, airy feel.
items.meta: Opposite Wat Phikun Thong · open daily 8.00–18.30

items.name: Cocochi Cafe
items.blurb: A Japanese-style cafe in town, with matcha, americano, strawberry soda and several kinds of cake. There are yukata sets to rent for photos, so it suits anyone who likes cute corners and wants a few shots to take home. It's in town and easy to reach.

blocks.title: Tips before you go
blocks.html: A lot of Sing Buri's prettiest cafes only open on weekends (Loychai Eye View, The Green). If you're coming on a weekday, aim for the in-town spots like Singkafe, Sip & Prost or Cocochi, which open daily instead. And always check a cafe's Facebook page before you set off — small upcountry cafes change their hours often.

blocks.text: Which Cafe to Pick by Your Plan

blocks.html: If you're doing a one-day Sing Buri trip, most of the cafes slot neatly into the temple-hopping route. We've grouped them so it's easy to choose based on where you're heading that day.

items.name: Temple & merit-making route
items.blurb: Retro Cafe at Wat Phikun Thong, or De'champ across from the temple — drop in straight after visiting, no need to drive far.

items.name: Nature & rice-field route
items.blurb: Rimna Cafe and WEEK in the Bang Rachan area, with green rice-field views — a good follow-up to the Bang Rachan camp and the Heroes' Monument.

items.name: In-town & market route
items.blurb: Singkafe, Sip & Prost and Cocochi sit in town and are easy to walk to, perfect to fit in between a bowl of boat noodles or a market stroll.

items: Morning 8.00–10.00 — the rice-field and garden cafes aren't hot yet, the views are lovely, the crowds are thin, and it's easy to take photos.
Afternoon 14.00–16.00 — time to rest your legs after morning temple-hopping; the sun softens and it's ideal to settle into an air-conditioned cafe.
Saturday–Sunday — several of the nicer cafes only open on weekends, so come on a weekend if you want to hit them all.

faq.q: Which Sing Buri cafes are open every day?
faq.a: In-town spots like Singkafe, Sip & Prost and Cocochi open daily, along with Vazana on the In Buri side, Rimna Cafe and De'champ. Loychai Eye View and The Green, on the other hand, only open on Saturdays and Sundays, so check the cafe's page before you go.

faq.q: Are there any riverside or waterside cafes in Sing Buri?
faq.a: Yes — The Green @ Singburi has clear waterside seating. For the rice-field nature feel, Rimna Cafe and De'champ both look out over the paddies, which are great for sitting and catching the cool breeze.

faq.q: How much do cafes in Sing Buri cost?
faq.a: Most coffees run 30–75 THB. The cheapest is Singkafe in the town market, starting at 30 THB, while the garden and riverside cafes sit around 50–75 THB — still friendly compared with the big tourist towns.

faq.q: Can I stop at a cafe while temple-hopping in Sing Buri?
faq.a: Easily. Retro Cafe at Wat Phikun Thong is inside the temple itself, while De'champ is right across from Wat Phikun Thong — you can sit down for a coffee at either straight after your visit. In the Bang Rachan area, Rimna and WEEK are close to the Bang Rachan camp.

faq.q: Can I see the temples and visit cafes in Sing Buri in a single day?
faq.a: Yes — it's a small town and the distances between spots are short. We'd suggest doing the temples in the morning before it gets hot, then dropping into cafes in the afternoon to rest your legs. You'll find the full itinerary in the Sing Buri travel guide.
